newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman's Sultan Qaboos decrees merger of two banks.
newsitem.headline: Oman's Sultan Qaboos decrees merger of two banks.

text.p: Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said on Wednesday approved the merger of two government-owned banks, the official Oman News Agency said.
The agency said Sultan Qaboos issued a decree approving the merger of the Oman Development Bank and Oman Bank for Agriculture and Fisheries to form the Omani Bank for Development.

"The merger is part of Oman's policy to encourage mergers of banking and financial institutions in the private and public sectors in order to strengthen their capital base and increase competitiveness," a banking official told Reuters.
He said the new bank would be open to private shareholders.

It was not clear what percentage of the new bank's shares would be offered to the public, but industry sources said the figure was likely to be at least 40 percent in compliance with Oman's public shareholding companies' law.
The decree said the new bank would take over assets and liabilities of the two merged banks and would continue to extend soft loans to the private sector.
